title: spec review: Active path 2: tool_disclosure active passes the minimal allowlist to Claude workers, with a bus-event escalation when a hidden tool is needed
spec:
Today (T-0802) tool_disclosure mode "active" is treated as shadow. Build the real active branch. Facts: spawn.run_worker builds the per-role Claude Code allowlist from the table at spawn.py:24-31 and passes it to the worker launch; tool_catalog.minimal_set(task, role) returns keep/drop/mandatory; Codex executors are untouched (their tools are the CLI's).
Do:
1. Active: when promotion.mode("tool_disclosure") == "active", run_worker passes the minimal set's `keep` list (mandatory always included) as the allowlist for review, spec_review, scout, challenge and the Claude execute fallback; the legacy full list is still logged in the tool_disclosure decision row as candidates, and the decision's selected becomes the kept list.
2. Escalation path (P11): the worker prompt gains one line telling the worker that if it needs a tool outside its allowlist it must post `bus_post_result` with status "held" and reason starting "needs_tool:<tool id>"; daemon (or spawn.run_worker's result handling) recognises that reason, records a decision_log row kind "tool_disclosure" reason "hidden_tool_requested", and re-spawns the worker once with the full legacy allowlist (respawn capped at one per task; the second attempt logs "tool_escalation_used" in the task pipeline). Scorecard: hidden_tool_recovery_rate per role = escalations / active spawns; `scorecard --economy` shows it.
3. Safety: mandatory tools (Read for all, Bash(git *) for review/scout, tests-green + Edit/Write for execute, bus_post_result for all) can never be dropped; a docs-only execute keeps Edit/Write.
Tests: tests/test_spawn.py::test_active_allowlist_is_minimal_set_with_mandatory, ::test_hidden_tool_request_respawns_once_with_full_allowlist; tests/test_tool_catalog.py::test_mandatory_never_dropped_in_active; docs/context-economy/06-tool-disclosure.md Active section with the revert path.
Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result. Never quote double-brace placeholder tokens literally.

risks.issue: run_worker's post-run branch for non-review roles (scout, challenge, execute-fallback) ends with bus.post_result(task_id, ..., "done") once run_claude exits 0, with no check of what the worker already posted mid-run. Only the review-role path (T-0139 guard) checks the existing posted result before overwriting. A worker that posts bus_post_result(status="held", reason="needs_tool:X") per P11 will have that status silently overwritten back to done before any respawn logic can see it.

dispatch()'s automatic held-retry loop (bus.read(status="held", role="execute") at line 741, re-armed at 866-871) only re-dispatches role==execute tasks. Held review/scout/challenge/spec_review tasks currently wait for Planner/human action (review_held_at, spec_review_held_at), not automatic daemon retry. The spec names no insertion point in daemon.py that reaches these non-execute roles, and doesn't reconcile the new auto-respawn with the existing held-waits-for-Planner convention.

pool.reserve()/max_budget_usd/timeout are computed once per run_worker() call before the first run_claude invocation. A one-time respawn implies a second full `claude -p` subprocess call for the same task, but the spec doesn't say whether that second call draws a fresh budget/timeout reservation or silently doubles spend and wall-clock against the single reservation already made.

The 'scorecard --economy shows it' claim depends on cli.py's `if a.economy:` block (not in scope), which prints only by_role_task_class, handoffs_by_executor_task_class, promotion, and last_context_eval. hidden_tool_recovery_rate is described as 'per role' which doesn't match the existing per-(role,task_class) structure context_scorecard.build() returns, so it's unclear whether it's visible for free or needs an unscoped cli.py change. No acceptance test covers this claim.

suggested_spec_changes: Name the exact hook in spawn.py's run_worker result handling (or a new helper called before the generic done/failed post_result branches) that checks bus.get(task_id)'s current status/hold_reason for a 'needs_tool:' prefix before that branch overwrites it, mirroring the existing review-verdict guard.

Either scope daemon.py changes to add a held-retry path for review/scout/challenge/spec_review roles analogous to the existing role==execute retry_held logic, or move the one-time respawn entirely into spawn.run_worker (synchronous, same call) and drop daemon.py from scope.

Specify budget/timeout handling for the respawned attempt: either reserve a second budget slot via pool.reserve() before the retry call, or cap the respawn's max_budget_usd/timeout so combined spend can't exceed the original per-task limit.

Either state that hidden_tool_recovery_rate is added as a key inside context_scorecard.build()'s existing by_role_task_class dict (so it appears in scorecard --economy without touching cli.py), or add orchestrator/cli.py to scope and give it an acceptance test.
